sentences.text: This revision petition has been filed challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence in a prosecution under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. The petitioner is the accused No.1 in C.C.No.1105/2014 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-IV, Kozhikode (for short, 'the trial court').

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-IV, Kozhikode
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He faced trial for the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

He was convicted for the offence under Section 420 of IPC alone and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for two years and to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/-, in default to suffer simple imprisonment for three months.
3. During the pendency of this revision petition, the revision petitioner died.

No legal heirs of the revision petitioner have come forward to prosecute the revision CRL.REV.PET NO. 626 OF 2021 :3 :
2025:KER:93954 petition.

The Supreme Court in Pranab Kumar Mitra v. State of W.B. [1959 KHC 463] has held that on the death of the revision petitioner during the pendency of the revision filed,
the revision shall not be abated and the revisional court has the power to examine the correctness of the conviction and sentence.

entities.text: Pranab Kumar Mitra v. State of W.B. [1959 KHC 463]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
A single Bench of this Court in Rev.Bishop K.M.Chacko v.
P.S.Jayaprakash and Another [2009 (3) KHC 67

entities.text:
Rev.Bishop K.M.Chacko v.
P.S.Jayaprakash and Another [2009 (3) KHC 67
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ), following the decision of the Supreme Court in Pranab Kumar Mitra (supra), held that on the death of the revision petitioner after filing of revision before the High Court invoking Sections 397 and 401 of Cr.P.C., the revision will not be abated and the High Court is bound to dispose of the revision on merits in accordance with law.

It was further held that even though the legal heirs have not come forward to pursue the revision, the jurisdiction of the High Court to decide the revision, after it has been taken on file, on its merits does not cease.
Heard Sri.A.Ranjith Narayanan, the learned counsel for the revision petitioner and Sri.E.C.Bineesh, the learned Senior Public Prosecutor and perused the entire records.

5. On going through the records, I am of the view that the trial court as well as the appellate court have gone through the entire evidence in the correct perspective and came to the conclusion that the revision petitioner had committed the offence under Section 420 of IPC and sentenced him to rigorous imprisonment.
It is settled that re-appreciation of evidence is not permissible in revision.
Hence, I see no reason to interfere with the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence.

6. For the reasons stated above, the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence stands confirmed.
Since the petitioner is no more, the substantive sentence has become inoperative.
The learned counsel for the petitioner CRL.REV.PET NO. 626 OF 2021 :5 : 2025:KER:93954 submitted that towards the fine amount, Rs.5,000/- has already been deposited.

The State is entitled to realise the balance amount of Rs.5,000/- from the legal heirs of the revision petitioner, in accordance with law.
